overall_summary: The channel achieves its highest view counts and retention when covering large-scale cosmic and planetary physics scenarios (e.g., Earth rings, atmosphere loss, speed of light changes). Microscopic, invisible, or niche material transformation topics (e.g., seeing Wi-Fi signals, sand turning to glass, liquid mercury water) consistently underperform in impression conversion and total view velocity.

what_is_working.evidence: 'What If Earth Had Rings Like Saturn?' reached 1,040 views with 51.26% average view percentage; 'What If Earth Lost Its Atmosphere for 5 Seconds?' reached 862 views.
what_is_working.action: Focus 80% of content production on high-stakes planetary physics, orbital anomalies, and fundamental physical constant changes.

what_is_working.evidence: 'What If the Speed of Light Dropped to the Speed of Sound?' generated 548 views, 40.89% APV, and sustained >60% audience watch ratio through 25% progress.
what_is_working.action: Formulate hypotheses that alter universal laws (gravity, light speed, sound propagation) to drive deep curiosity and watch duration.

what_to_improve.evidence: 'What If You Could See Every Wi-Fi Signal?' got 16 views; 'What If All Sand Turned to Glass?' got 19 views; 'What If Water Turned Into Liquid Mercury?' got 19 views.
what_to_improve.action: Eliminate micro-scale or invisible chemical transformation topics that fail to convey immediate visual stakes.

what_to_improve.pattern: Early Retention Drop in Fast-Paced Catastrophes
what_to_improve.evidence: 'What If Rain Fell at the Speed of a Bullet?' lost ~23% of audience watch ratio within the first 10% progress and dropped to 0.049 relative retention at 23% progress.
what_to_improve.action: Improve the initial 3-second hook with immediate visual context before introducing rapid narrative escalation.

retention_insights.drop_or_strength: Relative retention surges to 0.499 by 49% progress in 'What If Earth Suddenly Grew Massive Saturn-Like Rings?'.
retention_insights.evidence: Audience watch ratio stays at 1.07+ for the first 7% of video progress and builds relative retention continuously into the mid-video.
retention_insights.action: Deliver a dramatic visual reveal within seconds 0-3 and show second-order visual consequences at seconds 15-20.

retention_insights.drop_or_strength: Audience watch ratio drops sharply from 1.0513 at 1% progress to 0.7692 at 10% progress.
retention_insights.evidence: Relative retention collapses to under 0.10 by 8% progress in 'What If Rain Fell at the Speed of a Bullet?'.
retention_insights.action: Avoid text-heavy intro explanations; open directly with realistic CGI animation showing the terminal impact.

best_posting_windows.reason: Top performing upload time on 2026-09-05 produced the channel's highest view count (1,040 views) and watch time (257 minutes).
Yielded high initial view velocity with 'What If Earth Lost Its Atmosphere for 5 Seconds?' (862 views).
